skill.description: Builds and reviews responsive email HTML using table layouts, dark-mode safeguards, accessibility checks, image fallbacks, and client-specific render guidance.

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, repository-relative documentation links, and email-client terminology. The optional Resend command can execute a local connector and send email with the live flag, while the skill also directs persistent memory updates without an explicit approval gate.

remediation.issue: The optional Resend workflow includes a live command that can send email.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation immediately before execution, display the sender and recipients, and keep dry-run behavior as the default.

remediation.issue: Confirmed render blockers are promoted into persistent memory files without a clear approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before writing memory files, show the target paths and proposed content, and exclude untrusted pasted markup from persistent notes.

content.user_title: Build Responsive Email HTML Across Major Clients
content.value_statement: Email HTML often breaks across clients, dark mode, and image-blocking settings. This skill builds resilient layouts and reports expected rendering limitations.
actual_capabilities: Converts approved creative or supplied HTML into a single-column, table-based email layout with inline styles.
Applies responsive fluid or hybrid patterns for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, iOS Mail, and Android clients.
Reviews dark-mode contrast, semantic reading order, alt text, language attributes, and mobile font sizing.
Produces a client-render matrix with measured or estimated labels for each target client.
Creates image-off fallbacks, bulletproof buttons, and a plain-text alternate that matches the HTML message.
limitations: It does not write or silently rewrite subject lines, body copy, or CTA wording.
It cannot verify actual client rendering without a seed test or inbox-preview result.
Optional live test sends require a configured Resend connector and explicit user approval.
It does not score marketing quality, enforce SEND vetoes, or calculate EQS.

use_cases.title: Build a Campaign Email
use_cases.description: Turn approved campaign copy into responsive email HTML with accessible images, buttons, and plain-text parity.

use_cases.title: Repair Outlook Rendering
use_cases.description: Review an existing template, identify Outlook layout failures, and recommend compatible table, VML, and fallback patterns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client QA
use_cases.description: Create a labeled render matrix for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, iOS Mail, and Android before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Build Basic Email HTML
prompt_templates.prompt: Build responsive email HTML from this approved creative: [content]. Use this destination URL: [URL]. Preserve every word.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has approved copy and needs a reliable HTML build.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this email HTML for mobile layout, dark mode, image-off behavior, accessibility, and plain-text parity: [HTML].
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has a template and needs a structured QA report.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Client-Specific Defects
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the reported rendering defects in [clients]: [defects]. Keep the copy unchanged and explain each compatibility decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has measured failures from selected email clients.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Advanced Render Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production render plan for [mode] targeting [clients]. Include layout strategy, dark-mode rules, accessibility checks, fallbacks, and measured-versus-estimated labels.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs implementation guidance and a complete cross-client QA plan.

output_examples.input: Build a responsive promotional email for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, iOS Mail, and Android.
output_examples.output: A table-based email build is prepared with inline styles, a mobile reflow strategy, dark-mode safeguards, accessible images, and a matching plain-text version.

output_examples.input: Review this newsletter after Outlook desktop showed broken buttons and spacing.
output: Outlook desktop: fail, measured. Replace the CSS-only button with a VML-backed button.
Gmail web: estimated. Keep load-bearing styles inline.
Apple Mail: estimated. Review logo contrast under forced dark mode.

output_examples.input: Create a client QA matrix without access to a seed-list test.
output_examples.output: The matrix labels every client result as estimated, records known compatibility risks, and lists real render tests as open follow-up work.

best_practices: Provide approved copy, the destination URL, target clients, and brand constraints before requesting the build.
Use real seed or inbox-preview results to replace estimated matrix rows with measured evidence.
Review recipients and sender details before approving any live render-test email.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent campaign copy or change approved wording without review.
Do not present support-matrix estimates as measured client-render results.
Do not depend on external stylesheets, image-only CTAs, or unsupported modern layout features.

faq.question: Can this skill write the email copy?
faq.answer: No. It builds and reviews HTML from approved copy and reports wording changes that require separate review.

faq.question: Does it generate responsive email HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses table-based layouts, inline styles, constrained widths, and compatible mobile reflow patterns.

faq.question: Can it guarantee rendering in every email client?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes measured tests from estimates and identifies unknown behavior as follow-up work.

faq.question: Does it support dark mode and accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks color contrast, image alternatives, reading order, language attributes, link clarity, and mobile text sizing.

faq.question: Can it send a render-test email?
faq.answer: It can suggest an optional Resend connector command. A live send requires configured credentials, verified recipients, and explicit approval.

faq.question: Does it score email marketing quality?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the rendered unit and QA evidence, but a separate auditing workflow must perform quality scoring.
